findings.problem: BatchWorkflow uses pub status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool — any combination of these fields is legal, including impossible states like status="new" with is_sent=true, or status="sent" with is_sent=false
findings.failure_mode: Corrupted or partial updates produce logically inconsistent batch records that silently pass validation; downstream consumers cannot rely on status or boolean flags
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool with a single BatchStatus enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) and a typestate wrapper so sent-at is only constructable in the Sent state

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are primitive lifecycle booleans that encode a workflow state machine; they are orthogonal to status: String and can drift out of sync
findings.failure_mode: Booleans can be set independently of status string, allowing states like (status="validated", is_sent=true) or (status="", is_validated=false, is_sent=false) which violate domain invariants
findings.fix: Remove both bool fields; encode lifecycle transitions in a single enum or a typestate enum (BatchStatus::Pending | BatchStatus::Validated | BatchStatus::Sent)

findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary value (e.g., "SENT", "", "deleted", "pending2"); no domain discipline or exhaustive matching at the type level
findings.failure_mode: Typos, external input, or race-condition partial writes produce unrecognized status values that break downstream match/exhaustive checks; no compile-time guarantee of valid states
findings.fix: Replace with a non-exhaustive or exhaustive enum: pub enum BatchStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and derive Display for formatting

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership and mutates item.status and item.is_sent directly without any validation or atomic transition; caller can also mutate fields freely since all are pub
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent can be called when status is already "sent" or when the batch was never validated; no preconditions enforced, so the function is a blind state mutation
findings.fix: Replace with a fallible constructor or method on a typestate-aware enum: fn into_sent(self) -> Result<BatchWorkflow, BatchError> that checks the prior state and returns a typed error on invalid transitions

findings.problem: No typestate enum or state machine exists; the struct represents a workflow that should have a linear lifecycle (Pending → Validated → Sent) but the compiler cannot enforce ordering or prevent backward transitions
findings.failure_mode: Callers can skip Validated, re-validate, or unset sent state via direct field mutation; the lifecycle is enforced by convention, not the type system
findings.fix: Define an enum with ordered states and make transitions fallible; use associated functions like BatchWorkflow::validate() -> Result<BatchWorkflow, BatchError> and BatchWorkflow::send() -> Result<BatchWorkflow, BatchError>

findings.problem: id: String provides no domain typing; any string is accepted with no length, format, or uniqueness constraint enforced at the type level
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicated IDs, or malformed IDs pass silently; downstream lookups and dedup logic must re-validate raw string constraints
findings.fix: Introduce a BatchId newtype struct with a fallible constructor (fn new(s: &str) -> Result<BatchId, BatchError>) that enforces length/format rules

findings.problem: All fields of BatchWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to set any field directly, bypassing the type system entirely
findings.failure_mode: External callers can construct arbitrary invalid states without going through the type's constructors or transition methods
findings.fix: Make fields private (no pub) and provide constructor + transition methods that enforce invariants

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for mark_sent or any performance claim about the batch workflow
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify allocation behavior or performance characteristics of the typestate migration or transition methods
findings.fix: Add a criterion or minijohn benchmark for state transitions, especially after typestate migration

findings.problem: No profiler data (flamegraph, cachegrind, perf) exists to validate the hot path of the batch workflow
findings.failure_mode: Cannot confirm whether enum-based state transitions improve or degrade cache locality vs the current String-based approach
findings.fix: Run cargo flamegraph or perf record on representative batch processing workloads after typestate migration

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates via "sent".to_string() on every call; no allocation budget or measured claim about whether this is acceptable
findings.failure_mode: In a hot path processing thousands of batches, repeated String allocation for a constant literal is wasteful; enum-based status would eliminate all allocation
findings.fix: Replace with an enum variant (BatchStatus::Sent) which is zero-cost; if string representation is needed, derive Display on the enum

findings.problem: No second-ring test or integration evidence exists to validate the typestate migration preserves all expected behaviors
findings.failure_mode: Typestate migration could silently change transition semantics if not validated against integration test scenarios
findings.fix: Add integration/behavior tests covering all valid and invalid transition paths (Pending→Sent directly should fail, etc.)

findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify the crate compiles, passes tests, or meets clippy standards
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt, cargo clippy --workspace, and cargo test to establish baseline quality gates
